ana: Heads-up: aurorax13b (int4) canary started throwing warmstart OOMs after the midday ramp.

ana: Sample log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-24T11:02:12Z] OOM allocating 1.1GiB for kv_cache shard=0
model=aurorax13b-int4 host=canary-3 slot=0 prefetch=14 max_new_tokens=700
trace: kv_cache.rehydrate -> slab.grow -> memcpy -> OOM
```

mike: prefetch=14 + large max_new_tokens is a bad combo for mult-turn sessions. Fragmentation when slabs re-expand after evict explains OOMs.

sarah: quick mitigations to try on canary: drop prefetch to 2, set max_new_tokens=256, enable slab_compact_on_evict and soft_reserve. Also lower max_batch_size to 4.

ana: pushed a tiny canary defaults patch and rolled to 2/3 hosts:
```
model_defaults:
  max_new_tokens: 256
  prefetch: 2
  max_batch_size: 4
  slab_compact_on_evict: true
  soft_reserve: true
```

ops-bot: deploybot: Rolling update 6301234567 -> aurorax13b-int4 defaults patch started. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/models/aurorax13b/canaries/6301234567

mike: quick A/B (40m) after roll: OOM rate v1=13.7% -> v2=0.5%. p95 latency improved 130ms -> 95ms. memory peak down ~45%.

jon: ran a targeted quality eval on the 800-prompt benchmark: for prompts <2k tokens no measurable regression. For long-rollup set (>2.5k) we see truncation when generation hits cap; Rouge-L down ~1.2 points on 20 examples.

sarah: tradeoff expected. Plan: keep optimized defaults for primary pool and add a highmem variant routed for requests with estimated total_tokens > 2k. Also add runtime gauges kv_alloc_peak and slab_frag_pct; alert if kv_alloc_peak > 900MiB.

ana: filed infra ticket INFRA-3550 for metrics + routing rule and PR #954 for model defaults. Leaving canary open 24h, will promote if OOM <1% and long-rollup routing prevents regressions.

junior: (psst) maybe add an eval step that simulates eviction+rehydration patterns in CI to catch this earlier.

mike: +1, added to the model bring-up checklist. :thumbsup:
